source: CGZ arXiv:1712.04887v3 eqn (3), Lemma 2.4(b),(c), the relations on p. 2, Theorem 1.2; Addenda 33-34 (this repo)
scope: scope-(a) VALIDATION of the implementation behind Addenda 33-34, plus a CORRECTION to their stated value. Every check to date was internal, and a consistently-wrong P_zeta would have passed them all. Tested here against four CGZ predictions the implementation had no part in producing. ALL FOUR HOLD: Lemma 2.4(b) (D_zeta(1) = zeta mod cubes at n = 3, and D_zeta(1) = 3 (1 - zeta^2) exactly); Lemma 2.4(c) (kappa P(X) + kappa P(1/X) = 0 on 240 arguments); the reflection relation [X] + [1-X] - [0] = 0, which forces the NONZERO constant 2 mod 3 and ties the alpha-line symbols to each other via 1 - z_2 = alpha and 1 - z_1 = alpha^2; and the five-term relation of eqn (3) on 400 instances of a two-parameter sweep. Two constructed-to-fail controls -- one flipped sign, and zeta replaced by zeta^2 in a single factor -- break the sweep at 99/150 and 96/150, so the vanishing sum is the relation holding rather than a trivial class map. THE CORRECTION: the readout teich(u)^8 gives the class as a power of the mu_24 generator, not of zeta_3, and cls(zeta_3) = 2. Comparing it to a bare integer nearly produced a false report of a discrepancy with Lemma 2.4(b), and did produce a wrong basis label in Addenda 33-34: their 'eps_3 = zeta_3^2' should read eps_3(a[z_1] + b[z_2]) = zeta_3^{-a}, so eps_3(2[z_1] + [z_2]) = zeta_3. The structure those addenda report -- linearity, c_2 = 0, dependence on a alone -- is unaffected; only the basis label was wrong. Validates the implementation only; extends nothing to another place, field, or m. Nothing wired.
